title: AI Agents
lines: AI Agents teaches how to turn model suggestions into dependable working systems.
Its recurring teaching case follows a laboratory-device support problem as requirements accumulate.
The chapters connect memory, tools, evaluation, security, and economics through that evolving architecture.
You gain a way to decide how much autonomy a task actually needs.
The book treats deployment as an engineering commitment, rather than a conversational trick.

title: One incident, many obligations
lines: Meridian Instruments is a fictional teaching case about support for laboratory devices.
An incident requires evidence from accounts, telemetry, firmware, and internal knowledge.
As the system grows, earlier choices acquire memory, security, and coordination consequences.
The case makes those requirements appear for reasons the reader can follow.
It connects agent patterns with the work of operating a dependable service.

title: When work is interrupted
lines: The runtime chapters assume that processes crash and people answer later.
A checkpoint preserves meaningful task state so that work can resume.
Repeating an action requires care when its earlier attempt may already have changed something.
The book connects recovery with tool contracts, evidence, and operational evaluation.
Reliability becomes a property of the whole trajectory, rather than its final sentence.

title: Follow the evolving system
lines: Begin with Meridian's support problem and follow the architecture as obligations accumulate.
Use the evaluation chapters to question whether a convincing result demonstrates dependable work.
The economics chapters add supervision, deployment choices, and the costs surrounding model calls.
Later research possibilities remain distinct from the book's practical account of current engineering.
Read AI Agents to connect the decisions that a working agent system forces together.
